summary: Teams analyze financial data for a startup, prepare financial statements, calculate ratios, and present recommendations for funding strategies. Participants create a presentation justifying their recommendation using the provided financial data. Teams must follow all guidelines and present their findings to judges.
time_limits: No more than three (3) minutes setup in presentation room
No more than ten (10) minutes presentation time
No more than ten (10) minutes of judges’ questions
No more than five (5) minutes proctor orientation for state and national levels
No more than thirty (30) minutes preparation time for state and national levels
Presentation will be stopped at ten (10) minutes
submission_requirements: One (1) copy of the Works Cited, BPA Release Form(s), and AI Usage and Documentation Form for each round (prelims and finals)
Published and/or unpublished non-electronic written reference materials
deadlines: Teams must be registered for the national competition before the submission deadline
what_to_bring: Cordless calculator: Electronic devices will be monitored according to ACT standards. See NLC Calculator Guidelines. Contestants who violate this rule will be disqualified.
Optional: Easel, posters, graphs, poster board and/or flipcharts and markers and external displays will not be provided or permitted.
Students may use one single-sided laptop, notebook, or tablet for their presentation. Projection equipment and external displays will not be provided or permitted.
competencies: Apply accounting principles to evaluate and report the value of assets, liabilities, and owner’s equity in accordance with GAAP
Prepare, interpret, and analyze financial statements to assess performance and support strategic decision-making across various business models

Apply planning and control principles, including budgeting, forecasting, differential analysis, and present-value concepts, to evaluate organizational performance and guide financial decisions for both the short and long-term
Evaluate credit options, costs, and legal implications, and identify financial risks to inform business decisions and develop mitigation strategies
Communicate financial insights clearly, courteously, and professionally to diverse stakeholders
Use ratio analysis to evaluate comparative financial statements and assess organizational trends and performance
Apply statistical procedures and utilize spreadsheet software to analyze, interpret, and model financial data efficiently and accurately
Present financial findings using formal presentations and supporting materials to communicate insights and recommendations effectively

rubric.criterion: Team followed the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy.

rubric.description: Team maintains good eye contact, uses appropriate gestures and body language, and varies their tone and pace adequately.
Presentation content flows adequately, and each team member's role is clear and integrated into the presentation. Transitions between speakers and/or points are smooth.
Presentation demonstrates a good understanding of the topic and includes relevant and accurate information.
Fully integrated the additional information with insightful adjustments.
Responses are detailed, insightful, and effectively address the judges' questions.
Setup lasted no longer than three (3) minutes, presentation lasted no more than ten (10) minutes.
At least two original team members were present during the presentation.

judging_notes: AI Policy Level 2 Permitted with Citation
Carry-in and setup of equipment must be done solely by the team and must take place within the allotted time for orientation/warm-up
Business Professionals of America assumes no responsibility for hardware/software provided by the contestant
Finals may be required at state and national levels
Teams will be presented with an additional element to the scenario that requires revision of their final presentation
Judges’ comments will be returned digitally through the online judging system at the national level
eligibility_notes: Any secondary or postsecondary division contestant may enter this judged team event.
At least one (1) contestant should have an accounting background.
A team will consist of 2-4 contestants.
Teams must be registered for the national competition before the submission deadline and compete in both parts of the event to be ranked.
Entries that do not follow the provided topic or the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy will be disqualified.
Each state is allowed three (3) entries
